name: Ole Miss
title: University of Mississippi · Historic Core
place: The Lyceum · The Circle · The Grove

note.text: Mississippi’s spring brings a heightened threat of thunderstorms.
Mississippi has long, hot summers and high humidity.
The Grove’s canopy includes oaks, magnolias, and elms.
Mississippi winters are temperate, with cold spells generally short.

notes.title: Campus extent
notes.text: A 740 m square of the historic core and Grove, widened east to take in Lamar Hall. The stadium, western campus, and outlying university properties are beyond this scene.

notes.title: Measured terrain
notes.text: The ground is the real ground: bare-earth elevations from the 2018 USGS 3DEP lidar flight, drawn at true scale with no exaggeration. The historic core falls 22.8 m across the plot (134–157 m above sea level), with the Lyceum and Circle on the high ground. Contour lines are one metre apart, heavier every five; the cut edges of the plot show the profile. Use Contours to hide the lines.

notes.title: Measured roofs and heights
notes.text: 69 of 71 buildings carry measured roofs: a small set of planes read from the lidar returns over each OpenStreetMap footprint, so hips, valleys, dormers, penthouses and roof steps are the surveyed ones, and each wall rises to the eave the lidar saw. The Duff Center was built after the 2018 flight and keeps an interpreted height; the Student Union is shown as it stood during its 2018 expansion. Roof colours are sampled from the USDA NAIP aerial photograph.

notes.title: Surveyed trees
notes.text: The 1,012 trees stand where the lidar canopy shows them, with surveyed heights and crown widths: the Grove, the Circle and the street trees are the real pattern rather than a fill. Species, leaf colour and blossom are illustrative.

notes.title: Measured and illustrative
notes.text: Measured: building outlines, streets, paths and names (OpenStreetMap); ground, building heights, roof forms and tree positions (USGS lidar, 2018); roof colours (NAIP). Interpreted: wall colours, windows and trim on unstudied buildings, people, traffic, parking, weather and gameday layouts.

notes.title: Landmark studies
notes.text: Custom models of the Lyceum, Circle halls, observatories, and Fulton Chapel use mapped footprints and published descriptions. Details and heights without measurements are interpreted.

notes.title: A place in civil rights history
notes.text: James Meredith’s enrollment in 1962 is central to the historic district’s significance. The scene depicts everyday campus life.

notes.title: Explore the wider campus
notes.text: Use the campus-wide atlas for searchable main-campus buildings, playing fields, and streets beyond the miniature.

notes.title: Architectural detail pass
notes.text: Façades now distinguish arched and sash windows, stone lintels, cornices, gallery railings, column orders, and roof forms. Main elevations were compared with photographs. Minor dimensions and unseen elevations remain interpreted.

notes.title: Street life and wind
notes.text: Moving traffic, parked vehicles, bicycles, crowds, wind, and small façade projections are illustrative. Cars occupy mapped lanes and parking; extra festival crowds use open ground and closed roads. Gameday crowds gather in the Grove and Circle. These are atmospheric scenes rather than an attendance or parking survey.

notes.title: Ground and forecourts
notes.text: Paving, lawn, mulch and asphalt are drawn as materials, and the slopes are shaded from the measured terrain. The Student Union forecourts, the Walk of Champions and the Lamar Hall forecourt follow photographs and the aerial image; their exact dimensions, planting and furniture are approximate. Shrub beds along other buildings are illustrative.

note.text: The Walk of Champions passes through the Grove before home football games.
